D001_m001.question:
It’s been really noticeable for at least the last six months, but honestly, I’ve been like this since I was a kid—teachers always wrote that I “daydream” and “talk too much” on my report cards.

At work, I’m constantly struggling to keep things straight. Balancing drawers, tracking which customer needed what, remembering who I’ve already helped—my notes are all over sticky papers, and I still lose track. I start one task, then something else catches my eye, and I just abandon the first thing without meaning to. Even a coworker walking by or a random thought about what I’m making for dinner will pull my attention away.

I feel like I’m always in motion. On slow days at the bank, I can’t just sit; I’m tapping my foot, spinning in my chair, getting up to “straighten” the brochures. My coworkers joke that I never sit still. And I know I talk too much—I’ll start chatting with customers in line, oversharing or going off on tangents, and then realize I’ve held them up and feel embarrassed afterward.
D001_m001.options:

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

People tell me I never sit still. Even in meetings, I’m bouncing my leg, pacing, getting up to adjust something that doesn’t really need adjusting. I feel revved up all day, like there’s this motor running in the background. And I talk… a lot. I’ll launch into long explanations, interrupt people with ideas before they finish their sentence, then realize I’ve dominated the room.

Looking back, it’s not totally new. In school I was the kid staring out the window, tapping my pencil, getting told to “focus” or “quiet down” pretty much every day. It just feels like now it’s finally catching up with me.
